result.title: Which Way Is Up? Rotated Photos Silently Hurt Multi-View 3D Foundation Models
result.summary: Multi-view 3D foundation models estimate camera poses and 3D points from a set of photos in one forward pass. Many cameras store a portrait shot sideways, with an orientation tag telling viewers how to turn it, and this tag can be ignored, lost or wrong. We measure how rotated photos affect five such models on three datasets. A few rotated photos lower camera pose accuracy for every model, and the sideways photos already in a standard benchmark do the same. Even the most robust model still loses accuracy. The failure is also silent: the models' confidence does not reliably flag it, and most official image loaders ignore the tag. The fixes we test each correct only part of the problem. These findings call for orientation checks in reconstruction pipelines and benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文测量旋转照片（EXIF 方向标签被忽略、丢失或出错）对五个多视图 3D 基础模型在三个数据集上的相机位姿精度影响，发现少量旋转图片即造成精度下降，而模型置信度无法可靠报警，所测修复手段只能解决部分问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 「视觉输入被静默损坏而置信度不反映」这一发现，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「何时不应采信视觉输入」的可靠性判断提供旁证，其与推理期证据筛选的具体联系可供核查。
